full_name: Royal Ashdown Forest Golf Club (West Course)

summary.text: The West Course at Royal Ashdown Forest is a par 68 woodland course in East Sussex, bunker-free like the club's Old Course and once its ladies' course.

setting.text: The West snakes through the mature broadleaf woodland of the Ashdown Forest; the club says no earth was moved, no ponds dug and no streams diverted to build either course.
Short at 5,606 yards from the back tees, but far from flat, with small greens and severe run-offs that test the short game.
Ashdown Forest is protected by Acts of Parliament, so no alterations to the terrain are allowed without the conservators' approval.

history.text: The club was founded in 1888 as the Ashdown Forest & Tunbridge Wells Golf Club, by brothers William and Francis Lee, Robert Birch and the Reverend A. T. Scott. The course opened the following year.
Queen Victoria gave royal patronage in 1893, and Tunbridge Wells was dropped from the name in 1901.
There have been only five head professionals in the club's history, according to Top100golfcourses.

The ladies' course was enlarged to 18 holes in 1932, becoming the longest course in the country designed for ladies' golf; Cecil Leitch, Joyce Wethered, Diana Fishwick and Wanda Morgan played the opening exhibition.

Army training in the forest during the Second World War left only three or four holes in play by 1945. It was restored to 18 holes from 1965 with the Ashdown Forest Hotel, and the club took full control in 2003/4.
After the Ashdown Forest Hotel closed, the club renumbered the holes so the West starts and ends near the clubhouse.

trivia.text: Abe Mitchell, who lost the 1920 Open to George Duncan, was a member of the club's artisan section, the Cantelupe Club.
Winnie the Pooh's creator A. A. Milne and his son Christopher Robin were both members, Christopher playing mainly on the West Course.

11.text: A long par 3 that becomes a par 4 from the ladies' tees.

local.text: The forest is the setting for Winnie the Pooh. Top100golfcourses says Pooh invented Poohsticks on the edge of the woods.
The club's postcode is RH18, in East Sussex.
